content.intended_use: Obtain a nearby stationary witness; no algorithmic cost claim.

proofs.full_local_argument: Write F_x(z)=psi(z)+||z-x||^2/(2gamma) and m=1/gamma-rho>0. F_x is proper lower semicontinuous and m-strongly convex because F_x(z)=(psi(z)+rho||z||^2/2)+m||z||^2/2-<x,z>/gamma+||x||^2/(2gamma). Since psi is bounded below, F_x(z) tends to +infinity as ||z|| tends to infinity. A minimizing sequence is bounded; a convergent subsequence and lower semicontinuity give a minimizer u. Strong convexity makes it unique. For a strongly convex function with minimizer u, the inequality F_x(u+s(v-u))<=(1-s)F_x(u)+s F_x(v)-m s(1-s)||v-u||^2/2, combined with minimality and s decreasing to zero, gives F_x(v)>=F_x(u)+m||v-u||^2/2. Apply this to u=P(x), v=P(x+h), and also to F_{x+h} with its minimizer v. Adding the two inequalities and cancelling psi and quadratic terms gives m||v-u||^2<=<h,v-u>/gamma. Hence ||v-u||<=||h||/(1-gamma*rho). Evaluate F_{x+h} at u to get psi_gamma(x+h)-psi_gamma(x)<=<(x-u)/gamma,h>+||h||^2/(2gamma). Evaluate F_x at v to get the reverse bound psi_gamma(x+h)-psi_gamma(x)>=<(x-v)/gamma,h>+||h||^2/(2gamma). Their errors relative to <(x-u)/gamma,h> have magnitude bounded by a constant times ||h||^2 using the Lipschitz bound on v-u. Therefore psi_gamma is differentiable with gradient (x-u)/gamma, continuous because P is Lipschitz. Finally F_x(z)>=F_x(u) implies psi(z)>=psi(u)+<(x-u)/gamma,z-u>-||z-u||^2/(2gamma). The quadratic remainder is o(||z-u||), so (x-u)/gamma is a regular subgradient at u by the source definition. The distance inequality and norm identity follow immediately, and substitution of the epsilon bound proves the final implication. This proof uses no unreviewed scientific record as a dependency.

assumptions: psi is proper, lower semicontinuous and bounded below; psi(z)+(rho/2)||z||^2 is convex.
rho>=0 and gamma>0 satisfy gamma*rho<1. These explicit analytic conditions are the scope of the local argument; applying them to a new minimax marginal requires establishing them for that marginal.
statement.conclusion: P(x) exists and is unique; psi_gamma is continuously differentiable and grad psi_gamma(x)=(x-P(x))/gamma. Moreover (x-P(x))/gamma belongs to partial psi(P(x)), ||x-P(x)||=gamma||grad psi_gamma(x)||, and Dist(0,partial psi(P(x)))<=||grad psi_gamma(x)||. Thus ||grad psi_gamma(x)||<=epsilon implies a witness P(x) within gamma*epsilon of x with Dist(0,partial psi(P(x)))<=epsilon.
statement.objects_and_definitions: Let psi:R^p -> R union {+infinity}. All norms here are Euclidean. Define psi_gamma(x)=inf_z {psi(z)+||z-x||^2/(2gamma)} and P(x)=argmin_z of the same objective. partial psi denotes the regular subdifferential defined on PDF p.5; for a weakly convex function the convex quadratic shift also identifies it with the limiting subdifferential. Dist(0,S)=inf_{v in S}||v||.
statement.parameter_domains: p is a positive integer; rho>=0; gamma>0 with gamma*rho<1, including arbitrary finite gamma>0 if rho=0.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every x in R^p, deterministically; the epsilon implication holds for every epsilon>=0.
